title: A finite counterexample for strict consecutive totient patterns
abstract: Formalizes the finite counterexample at cutoff 826 from Proposition 1.2 of Przemek Chojecki's Consecutive Totient Patterns. With ranks assigned to positions and an inclusive cutoff, every strict length-three permutation occurs, no increasing length-four block occurs, and a decreasing length-four block does occur. Hence the largest universal length is three and decreasing is not always absent at the first non-universal length. This is a partial negative result for a specified reading of Erdos Problem 415; no novelty, asymptotic result or natural weak-order frequency result is claimed.
